marble.name: What Living Things Need
marble.subject: Science
marble.description: Understand what plants and animals (including humans) need to survive: water, food, air, and suitable conditions
marble.prompt: If you ask you what a pet dog or a garden plant needs to stay alive, can they list the basic things like water, food, and air?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning about the amazing diversity of life — identifying different animals and plants, understanding how body parts help animals survive, and discovering what all living things need to stay alive.

misconceptions: 'Plants get their food from the soil' — treating soil/water as food and missing that plants make food from light.
Assuming plants and animals need the SAME things (e.g. that plants need to be 'fed' food, or that animals photosynthesise).
Thinking a need is optional or cosmetic rather than survival-critical, because consequences are slow and unseen.
Confusing 'want' with 'need' (a pet 'needs' a toy) — not distinguishing survival needs from comforts.
representations: Split-plant fair test: identical plants, one given water/light, one deprived, observed over a week.
Two parallel 'need charts' side by side — animal needs vs plant needs — to make the contrast visible.
A care/keep-alive scenario (windowsill or terrarium) where each need is a supply the child provides.
Need → consequence pairing cards ('no water → wilts', 'no food → weak', 'no light → pale').
authoredAnswer: It won't grow well — it's missing light. Plants need light (as well as water, air and a suitable temperature); without light the plant goes pale, weak and eventually dies, because water alone isn't enough. Living things suffer if any one of their basic needs is missing.
probe: Grow two identical seedlings with equal water — one on a bright windowsill, one shut in a dark cupboard — for a week. Before the week passes, ask the child to predict whether the dark one will grow as well as the light one, and WHY. wrongAnswers.wrong: It will be fine — as long as a plant has water it will grow
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: says the watered plant will be fine in the dark
wrongAnswers.fix: list all a plant's needs — water, light, air, suitable temperature — and show light is essential using a dark-grown seedling

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: on the probe says soil is the plant's food and light isn't needed
wrongAnswers.fix: at this age, establish that plants need light to grow and make food; soil gives water and support, it isn't 'food'

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: omits air from a plant's needs
wrongAnswers.fix: include air among plant needs, alongside animals'
distinguish universal needs (water, air, food/light, suitable conditions) from human-specific wants
